x: In the 1 mile, John Burr ran well to finish 2nd to Eddie Ellis, of T.V.H., while in the 880 yds. Bob Taylor was also 2nd to Don McMillan, the Australian Olympic runner.

Archie Bedford on the 10th also did the fastest time of the day and brought us within striking distance of T.V.H. but Len Bishop on the last leg could make no impression on Eddie Ellis, T.V.H's International Steeplechaser, and the positions remained unchanged to the end.

Charlie Walker set off on the second leg in great style with Eddie Ellis of TVH breathing down his neck. These two battled throughout and soon disposed of Walton, Blackheath and Highgate but Ealing represented by Blagrove, Brighton with Briault, and Woodford with Chapman were making faster progress…

In those early halcyon days he beat most of his contempories - names like George Knight, Peter Driver, Ken Harland, Eddie Ellis, Jack Heywood and Ian Boyd - and, no doubt, he is tempted at times to think of what might have been.
